response.message:
We're building a cited Q&A assistant on AWS over a small synthetic document collection. It uses keyword retrieval that checks each source's permissions, an authenticated web app, and Amazon Bedrock as the model. I've drawn the full path from sign-in through retrieval to the model.

For the first test, we'd run Outputs → Emulate locally. That runs the generated code against simulated AWS services and scripted model replies. It can check the permission filtering, citations, abstaining on unsupported questions, the effect of updates and deletions, and suppressing an answer when access is revoked mid-generation. It can't show real Bedrock answer quality, IAM enforcement, real sign-in or deployment. Those need a later run in a real AWS account with model access you've confirmed.

Nothing has been deployed, and no region or account access has been approved. Which country does the synthetic data and its processing need to stay in, so we can pick an AWS region where your chosen Bedrock model is actually offered?

proposal.title: AWS bounded keyword RAG with authenticated web app
proposal.body: Scope: this is an architecture qualification using synthetic documents only. A browser user reaches the web app through CloudFront. The app signs users in with Cognito (authorization code with PKCE, plus MFA). Questions go through API Gateway, which checks the sign-in token, to a Lambda function. The Lambda does permission-aware keyword retrieval from a DynamoDB catalog and calls Bedrock through the Converse API. Ingestion: an operator loads the source documents and their explicit access lists using the generated catalog management tool. Assumptions: retrieval is keyword-based, not vector search. The Bedrock model ID, region, account and model access are all still unverified. Nothing has been deployed.

data.label: Signed-in user (browser)
data.description: A person using a browser. This is an external client reference, not a provisioned service.

data.label: Web app
data.description: Serves the web app from private S3 assets that only CloudFront can read. Handles sign-in with authorization code + PKCE and calls the API with an access token. Shows cited answers, or an abstention when the sources don't support an answer.

data.label: User sign-in
data.description: User pool with admin-created users, required software-token MFA and an access-token scope. Each user's identity and employee-region mapping comes from the catalog.

data.label: Authenticated RAG API
data.description: Bounded authenticated endpoint. A JWT route serves the browser. There is no anonymous access, and unknown identities fail closed.

data.label: Retrieval & answer function
data.description: Does keyword retrieval, filtering by each document's access list and region before anything reaches the model. Re-checks revisions and authorization after generation, so an answer is suppressed if access was revoked. Returns the answer with citations to current revisions, or abstains. Owns its execution role, logs, version and alias.

data.label: Document & permissions catalog
data.description: Holds up to 100 small synthetic UTF-8 documents with their revisions, explicit access lists and identity mappings. An operator ingests, updates and deletes documents using the generated management tool. Callers can't write to it.

data.label: Foundation model
data.description: A direct foundation model called through Converse. The model ID, region support, access and quotas are still to be selected and verified. Local emulation uses scripted responses only.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Prevents restricted content from leaking through generated answers.
requirementDrafts.basis: User acceptance criterion: "Denied documents never reach the model".
requirementDrafts.statement: Documents the user isn't allowed to read are filtered out before the model call and never reach it.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Lets users verify an answer and avoids citing stale content.
requirementDrafts.statement: Answers to known questions cite the current revision of each source document they use.
When no permitted source supports an answer, the system abstains instead of generating one.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Stops retrieval from serving content that has been removed or replaced.
requirementDrafts.statement: Updates and deletions in the catalog change what retrieval returns.

requirementDrafts.rationale: Closes the gap between the permission check and delivering the answer.
requirementDrafts.statement: If a user's access is revoked while an answer is being generated, that answer is suppressed.

response.message:
Good news: both local checks passed on design revision 2. They were "Stateful emulator resource setup" and "Generated retrieval, conditional writes, ACLs, updates, deletion and revocation". That's local evidence that the generated code handles permission filtering, updates, deletions and revocation, using simulated AWS services and scripted model replies. It doesn't prove IAM enforcement, real sign-in or MFA, API Gateway or CloudFront behaviour, how good real Bedrock answers are, or that anything can be deployed. I don't see a design defect to fix, so the board stays as it is.

The biggest open gap is that we haven't picked a country or region. Without one we can't check that your Bedrock model is actually offered there or run a provider-validated Terraform plan. Which country do the synthetic data and its processing need to stay in?
